title: Incremental traffic attenuation controller for hosted API regional rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a traffic attenuation controller that applies configurable decay curves to traffic weights during regional and cross-region rollouts for the Hosted API. The goal is to provide a predictable, SLO-driven gradual ramp with automated hold points and an emergency attenuation (quick-decay) path that reduces blast radius while keeping latency and availability SLOs protected.
plan: 1) Finalize attenuation model and config surface (linear, exponential, stepped). 2) Implement controller that integrates with the rollout orchestration service (orchestrator) to adjust region weights on the gateway. 3) Add SLO evaluation hooks (p99 latency, error_rate, token_throttle) and automated hold/rollback triggers. 4) End-to-end test in staging with synthetic traffic and chaos injection. 5) Instrument dashboards and rollout runbook. 6) Ship with feature flag and guardrails for first 2 production rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can apply at least three attenuation curves (linear, exponential, stepped) via config
Rollouts show weight changes on the routing dashboard matching attenuation curve within 5% of expected values
Automated hold triggers fire when p99 latency increases by >25% or error_rate increases above 0.5% during a ramp
Emergency attenuation endpoint reduces traffic to a safe baseline within 30s and completes within 2 minutes
Smoke tests pass in staging with synthetic traffic under chaotic node failure scenarios
Playbook and dashboard created and linked; first production rollouts use feature flag and SRE signoff
